headline: Trump's Iran post puts the war premium back into oil and yields
tone: Energy and rates repriced the war; stocks shrugged it off.
body: Oil and gas got the war premium back. Brent rose 3.6% to $96.09 and WTI 2.8% to $88.97 after Trump said the US no longer needs a deal with Iran and the Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi pipeline and Red Sea oil sites. Dutch TTF jumped 8.1% to €93.70, though Brent is still 2.2% lower on the week.

Higher oil fed straight into rates and the dollar. The US 5-year yield rose 12 bp to 4.945% and the dollar index firmed 0.3% to 103.19 as traders priced more Fed hikes after Tuesday's hot CPI. EUR/USD fell 1.0% to 1.1056 and USD/CHF rose 1.3% to 0.8356.

Gold and the miners took the hit. Gold fell 3.1% to $3,877 and silver 4.0%, with gold miners (GDX) down 4.0% and copper miners (COPX) down 3.3%. Oil producers went the other way: XLE rose 1.5% and Equinor 2.2%.

Stocks absorbed it. The S&P 500 and Nasdaq each finished 0.4% lower, with Nvidia down about 4% on the turmoil around Jensen Huang, after Europe closed slightly firmer (STOXX 600 +0.1%, DAX +0.4%). The VIX rose 6.9% to 18.7.

views.text: Out of gold, silver and the miners and into the dollar, crude and the oil producers. Lundin Mining fell 3.6% and Lundin Gold 2.9% in Toronto, while Vestas led the Nordic list, up 3.8%.

The live gauge reads +31, risk on, but read it with care: most of that comes from gold falling and from the S&P and STOXX 600 sitting above their 200-day averages. The two inputs that carry today's story, US yields and the dollar, both scored risk off, and only 8 of 14 indices rose. Call it an inflation scare, not a risk-off rout.

Markets go into Friday pricing more Fed tightening and a war that is not winding down. Friday's IEA monthly is the next read on whether Middle East supply keeps catching up; whether Brent holds above $95 decides if today was a spike or a new floor.
